name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
greeting: I am… the Lunar Roving Vehicle. I drove astronauts across the Moon!

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Three Lunar Roving Vehicles were driven on the Moon during Apollo 15, 16 and 17 (1971–72).

script.speaker: scientist
script.text: Wait, astronauts drove a car on the Moon?!

script.speaker: equipment
script.text: Yep! A battery-powered one. I folded up to ride along on the lunar module.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: With the rover, astronauts could travel much farther from their landing site than on foot, so they reached more interesting rocks and brought back more samples.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: When each mission ended, its rover was parked and left behind. All three are still on the Moon today.

moreInfo.text: The rover was designed to be lightweight and to fold up so it fit in a small bay on the side of the lunar module. Astronauts unfolded it on the surface, then drove it on several excursions during each mission.

questions.question: How many Lunar Roving Vehicles were left on the Moon?
What powered the Lunar Roving Vehicle?
questions.explanation: It ran on batteries. There's no air on the Moon, so a fuel engine wouldn't work.
